name: Hadamard as an H-box
summary: An arity-2 H-box with the standard label is √2 times a Hadamard gate.
description:
The arity-2 H-box with label $-1$ is the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix} = \sqrt 2\,H$. This is why H-boxes are called H-boxes: they generalise the Hadamard gate to any number of legs. Hence a Hadamard gate (drawn on the right as a Hadamard edge) can always be translated into an H-box and back.

Because of this, ZH-diagrams often draw an arity-2 H-box and a Hadamard gate in the same way, ignoring the factor $\sqrt 2$.

source.location: Section 2.1, translation of the Hadamard gate

notes: The H-boxes here are *unnormalised*: an H-box with label $a$ has all entries equal to $1$, except for the entry where all wires are $1$, which is $a$. The grey spiders of the ZH papers are normalised differently from the X-spiders of PyZX, so scalar factors may differ from those in the papers.
